articleSummary: As of June 13, 2026, the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has reported 710 confirmed cases of Ebola, resulting in 139 deaths, primarily in Ituri province. The outbreak, attributed to the Bundibugyo strain, has affected 29 health zones, with a concerning increase of 17 new cases and five deaths in just one day. The ongoing humanitarian crisis complicates response efforts, with 7.8 million people displaced and 26.5 million facing acute food insecurity. A critical shortage of isolation beds and a $21.5 million funding gap further exacerbate the situation. Community mistrust has severely limited contact tracing, with only about 6,000 of an estimated 20,000 contacts reached. The World Health Organization (WHO) has declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern due to the risk of cross-border transmission to Uganda, which has reported 19 confirmed cases linked to the DRC outbreak. A $518 million preparedness and response plan has been initiated to enhance surveillance and health system responses, marking this outbreak as the fourth-largest in Africa.
notes: WHOによるPHEIC宣言済み。確認症例710名、死亡139名。Bundibugyo株による流行。隣国ウガンダへの越識感染（確認症例19名）が既に発生。資金不足（21.5百万ドルのギャップ）、人道的危機（780万人の避難民、2650万人が食料不安に直面）、コミュニティの信頼喪失によるコンタクトトレーシング困難など、深刻な対応阻害要因が存在。アフリカ第4位規模の流行として特に注視が必要。

The detection originated from a sample taken at the Vijay Nagar sewage pumping station on June 5, leading to the mapping of drainage networks and identification of affected areas, including Bulandshahr and Shastri Nagar, which have been fully surveyed. Other localities involved are Raj Nagar, Daulatpura, and several others, impacting around 150,000 residents. The Uttar Pradesh government, in collaboration with the NCDC and WHO, is overseeing the survey. Officials report that the detected strain is largely non-virulent and contained, with similar instances previously noted in Varanasi and Meghalaya. VDPVs are rare occurrences that may indicate low immunity levels and are typically traced back to the oral polio vaccine through environmental surveillance.
notes: VDPVは遺伝子的にまれな発生であり、低いワクチン免疫水準を示唆する可能性がある。記事では現在のところ確定患者報告がなく、検出株は「非毒性」と表現されているが、下水検出の継続的な監視とその公衆衛生的な意味合いは要注視。インド当局、NCDC、WHOが関与しており、政府の関心度は高い。

articleHeadline: Dengue in Brazil: Severe cases highlight healthcare challenges and recovery efforts
articleSummary: In Brazil, a 25-year-old patient, Ruan Lincoln Nunes, faced life-threatening complications from dengue hemorrhagic fever, including abdominal hemorrhage, septic shock, and respiratory failure. Transferred to Hospital Regional Dr. Abelardo Santos in Belém, Pará, he underwent extensive ICU treatment, including surgery, intubation, and multiple blood transfusions. After a cardiac arrest and subsequent resuscitation, he gradually improved over two weeks, eventually weaning off mechanical ventilation and resuming normal feeding. This case underscores the critical role of multidisciplinary care and community support in managing severe dengue cases. The hospital, which has 40 ICU beds, reports an average of 154 admissions monthly, reflecting ongoing challenges in addressing dengue's impact on public health.
notes: 記事は25歳患者の単一症例のICU治療経過を詳細に報告しており、重症度（デング出血熱、敗血性ショック、呼吸不全）が高い。病院の月平均入院数154件からデング負担が継続していることが示唆されるが、全国的な流行状況や症例数の増加傾向を示す情報は明記されていない。IHR基準では『異常/予想外』に該当しない（ブラジルにおけるデング重症例は周知の事実）。国際的拡大の兆候もない。従ってWATCH段階で経過観察が適切と判定。

articleHeadline: Botulism in Brazil: Zoo reopens after botulism outbreak investigation
articleSummary: Sapucaia do Sul Zoo in Brazil reopened on June 13 after a month-long closure due to suspected avian influenza. During the closure, 36 birds died, including 22 Black-necked swans and 11 Black swans. Laboratory tests ruled out Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza and Newcastle disease, with botulism identified as the cause of death on June 9. The zoo has implemented improvements in water quality and monitoring to prevent further incidents. No new deaths have been reported in the two weeks leading up to the reopening, and authorities are maintaining strict animal health surveillance and biosafety protocols to ensure visitor safety.
